trial_court: Principal Judge, Family Court, SBS Nagar (T.A.No. 1420 of 2022)
acts_cited_auto: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

acts_cited.act: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

facts_of_case: Parties were married in 2020. No child was born. Petitioner-wife is living separately since 28.3.2022 and seeking transfer of respondent-husband's petition under Section 13 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.

legal_principles.principle: The ends of justice should demand the transfer of the suit, appeal or other proceeding.
legal_principles.held: The cardinal principle for exercise of power under section 24 of the Code of Civil Procedure is that the ends of justice should demand the transfer of the suit, appeal or other proceeding.
cited_cases: N.C.V. Aishwarya vs A.S. Saravana Karthik Sha, (2022) Live Law (SC) 627

legal_principles.principle: In matrimonial matters, the Courts have to take into consideration the economic soundness of both parties, their social strata, behavioural pattern, standard of life prior to and subsequent to marriage.
legal_principles.held: In matrimonial matters, wherever Courts are called upon to consider the plea of transfer, the Courts have to take into consideration the economic soundness of both the parties, the social strata of the spouses and their behavioural pattern, their standard of life prior to the marriage and subsequent thereto and the circumstances of both the parties in eking out their livelihood.
cited_cases: N.C.V. Aishwarya vs A.S. Saravana Karthik Sha, (2022) Live Law (SC) 627

legal_principles.principle: The Courts should give more weightage and consideration to the convenience of female litigants while deciding transfer applications.
legal_principles.held: Further, when two or more proceedings are pending in different Courts between the same parties which raise common question of fact and law, and when the decisions in the cases are interdependent, it is desirable that they should be tried together by the same Judge so as to avoid multiplicity in trial of the same issues and conflict of decisions.
applicable_acts_sections: Code of Civil Procedure — Section X
cited_cases: Sumita Singh vs Kumar Sanjay, (2002) SC 396
Rajani Kishor Pardeshi vs Kishor Babulal Pardeshi, (2005) (12) SCC 237

legal_principles.principle: The Courts should consider the family condition of the wife, custody of minor child, economic condition of the wife, her physical health and earning capacity of the husband while deciding transfer applications.
legal_principles.held: Accordingly, it is well settled that while considering the transfer of a matrimonial dispute/case, at the instance of the wife, the Court is to consider the family condition of the wife, the custody of the minor child, economic condition of the wife, her physical health and earning capacity of the husband.
cited_cases: Sumita Singh vs Kumar Sanjay, (2002) SC 396
Rajani Kishor Pardeshi vs Kishor Babulal Pardeshi, (2005) (12) SCC 237

outcome.final_order: Transfer of case granted to a Court of competent jurisdiction at Ambala (Haryana).
